question: Direction: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate set of words to make the sentence contextually and grammatically meaningful. || Question: By attempting to ______ the opposing factions with vague promises, the mediator ended up pleasing no one; his ______ approach was seen not as diplomatic grace, but as moral ______.

question: Direction: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate set of words to make the sentence contextually and grammatically meaningful. || Question: Despite being initially touted as a ______ for the nation’s deep-rooted economic malaise, the newly implemented fiscal policy proved to be highly ______, ultimately ______ the already alarming wealth gap.

question: Direction: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate set of words to make the sentence contextually and grammatically meaningful. || Question: Rather than offering a ______ analysis of the social crisis, the author’s latest book is little more than a partisan ______, completely devoid of the ______ that characterized his earlier, more respected works.

question: Direction: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate set of words to make the sentence contextually and grammatically meaningful. || Question: The CEO’s public apology felt entirely ______, delivered with a robotic cadence that revealed a staggering lack of ______ for the massive ecological disaster caused by his corporation's ______ negligence.

tip: Historical accounts mein 'sanitized' ka matlab hota hai unplesant facts (jaise barbarity) ko hata dena.

question: Direction: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate set of words to make the sentence contextually and grammatically meaningful. || Question: Environmentalists warn that the current international accords are merely ______, offering empty promises while the ______ destruction of global ecosystems pushes the planet closer to an irreversible ______.
explanation: Accords (agreements) ko 'merely' kaha gaya hai, yani wo sirf upari dikhawa/make-up (cosmetic) hain. Dusri taraf destruction bina ruke, jise taala na ja sake (inexorable) lagatar badh raha hai. Ye destruction planet ko ek aisi khaai ya tabahi (abyss) ki taraf dhakel raha hai jahan se wapsi namumkin (irreversible) hai. 'stringent' matlab strict, jo 'empty promises' se contradict karega.
trick: Empty promises = cosmetic/superficial. Destruction jo nahi ruk raha = inexorable. Irreversible aakhri stage hai, jo hamesha negative hogi = abyss (khaai).
tip: Inexorable ka matlab hai relentless, unstoppable. Palliative (temporary relief) theek tha, par sporadic (ruk-ruk kar) destruction ki intensity ko kam kar deta hai.

question: Direction: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate set of words to make the sentence contextually and grammatically meaningful. || Question: The elite social club was governed by a strict code of extreme politeness, but this immaculate ______ merely served to disguise the deeply ______ gossip that circulated among its affluent members.
explanation: Social club mein extreme politeness thi, par wo sirf ek upari parat ya dikhawa (veneer/facade) thi. Asal mein wo log andar hi andar bahut buri aur zehreeli (malicious) gossip karte the. 'core, benign' bilkul ulta hai. 'facade' theek hai par uske sath 'altruistic' (selfless) gossip nahi ho sakti, gossip negative hi hogi context ke hisab se.
trick: 'Merely served to disguise' (sirf chhupane ke kaam aaya). Kya chhupayega? Bahar ki politeness andar ki burai (malicious gossip) ko chhupayegi. Veneer (thin outer layer) perfect word hai.
tip: Veneer of politeness hamesha malicious intent ya gossip ko mask (disguise) karne ke liye use hota hai.

question: Direction: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate set of words to make the sentence contextually and grammatically meaningful. || Question: Initially ______ as a groundbreaking medical breakthrough, the treatment was later exposed as entirely ______, leading to the rapid retraction of the study and the total ______ of its lead researcher.
explanation: Shuru mein us treatment ki bohot taareef (heralded) hui thi ek breakthrough ki tarah. Par baad mein pata chala ki wo poori tarah se jhootha/fake (spurious) tha. Iski wajah se study wapas leni padi aur main researcher ki bohot badnami / bezati (ignominy) hui. 'derided' matlab mazak udana, agar pehle mazak udata toh 'breakthrough' kyu kehte?
trick: 'Initially [positive]... later exposed as [negative]... leading to [negative result]'. Is structure ko map karo. Heralded (praised) -> Spurious (fake) -> Ignominy (public shame).
tip: Ignominy is a high-frequency word for public shame or disgrace, often following a scandal.

question: Direction: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate set of words to make the sentence contextually and grammatically meaningful. || Question: The economist sharply criticized the government's trickle-down policy, describing it as an ideological ______ that benefits the ultra-rich while leaving the working class mired in perpetual ______.
explanation: Economist trickle-down policy (ameero ko tax cut dene ki policy) ko buri tarah criticize kar raha hai. Usne ise ek illusion ya jhoothi umeed (chimera) kaha jo sirf ameeron ka bhala karti hai aur working class ko hamesha ke liye garibi/kangaali (destitution) mein dhakel deti hai. 'panacea' (cure-all) positive word hai jo 'sharply criticized' ke context me galat ho jayega.
trick: Criticism hai toh policy ek jhooth (chimera/illusion) hogi. 'Mired in perpetual' (hamesha ke liye fasa hua) ke baad obviously garibi (destitution) hi aayegi, affluence (ameeri) nahi.
tip: Chimera ka literal matlab ek mythical monster hota hai, par abstract English mein iska matlab 'an illusion or impossible dream' hota hai.

question: Direction: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate set of words to make the sentence contextually and grammatically meaningful. || Question: The philosopher argues that morality is not a universal truth but a highly ______ construct, shaped entirely by the cultural ______ of the ruling class to maintain their ______ grip on society.
explanation: Philosopher kehta hai ki morality (sahi-galat) koi fixed/universal truth nahi hai, balki wo subjective (har kisi ke hisab se alag) hai. Ise society ke powerful/ruling class apni dominance/power (hegemony) ke hisab se banate hain, taaki unka society par control poori tarah se (absolute) bana rahe. 'objective' aur 'immutable' universal truth ke synonyms hain, jo 'not a' ke baad nahi aayenge.
trick: 'Not a universal truth' clearly dictates that the first blank must be 'subjective' or 'relative'. The ruling class always uses its dominance ('hegemony') to maintain strong ('absolute') control.
tip: Hegemony ka matlab hai leadership or dominance, especially by one state or social group over others.

question: Direction: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate set of words to make the sentence contextually and grammatically meaningful. || Question: The media outlet was widely accused of yellow journalism, prioritizing ______ headlines designed to maximize engagement while completely ignoring the deeply ______ realities of the geopolitical conflict.
explanation: Yellow journalism ka matlab hai sensationalism (sansani-khez khabre). Outlet par aarop tha ki wo aisi bhadkili aur sensational (lurid) headlines use karte hain taaki clicks milein. Is chakkar mein wo conflict ki gahri, complex aur multi-layered (nuanced) sachai ko ignore kar dete hain. 'informative' aur 'muted' sensationalism ke opposite hain.
trick: Maximize engagement (clicks) ke liye headlines humesha 'lurid' (shocking/sensational) hoti hain. In headlines mein kabhi 'nuance' (subtle detail/complexity) nahi hota.
tip: Lurid headlines matlab aisi khabre jo deliberately shocking, violent ya sensationalized hoti hain.

question: Direction: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate set of words to make the sentence contextually and grammatically meaningful. || Question: The so-called peace summit was ultimately revealed to be a cynical ______, as both nations used the ceasefire not to negotiate, but to rapidly rearm for even more ______ and devastating ______.
explanation: Peace summit ko 'so-called' (naam-matra ka) aur 'cynical' kaha gaya hai. Ye ek dhokha/natak (charade) nikla. Dono deshon ne ceasefire ka use shanti ke liye nahi, balki hathiyar jama karne (rearm) ke liye kiya, taaki aur bhi zyada aggressive/ladaku (belligerent) dushmani aur ladaai (hostilities) shuru kar sakein. 'triumph' (jeet) positive hai jo yahan fit nahi hota.
trick: Rearming (hathiyar jama karna) ka direct effect ladaai (hostilities) hoga. 'Belligerent' (aggressive/warlike) perfectly modifies the word hostilities.
tip: Jab peace talks fake hon, toh unhe diplomat bhasha me 'charade' ya 'sham' kaha jata hai.

question: Direction: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate set of words to make the sentence contextually and grammatically meaningful. || Question: The new corporate headquarters, a massive, imposing glass structure, was heavily criticized as a ______ eyesore that stood deeply ______ with the delicate, historic architecture of the surrounding neighborhood.
explanation: Nayi building ek 'massive, imposing' structure hai, jise 'eyesore' (aankho ko chubhne wala) kaha gaya hai. Ek bahut bade aur solid structure ko 'monolithic' kehte hain. Ye building aas-paas ke nazuk (delicate) aur purane architecture ke sath bilkul mail nahi khati (incongruous/bemail). 'delicate, harmonious' poore tone ke opposite hai.
trick: 'Massive, imposing' ka synonym first blank (monolithic) me chahiye. Aur 'criticized as an eyesore' matlab aas-paas ke environment ke sath mismatch (incongruous) ho raha hai.
tip: Incongruous ka matlab hai out of place or mismatched with the surroundings.

question: Direction: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate set of words to make the sentence contextually and grammatically meaningful. || Question: The psychologist argued that excessive nostalgia is a deeply ______ trap; by obsessively yearning for a highly ______ version of the past, individuals condemn themselves to psychological ______ in the present.
explanation: Psychologist kehta hai ki purani yaadon me khona (nostalgia) ek lubhawna (seductive) jaal/trap hai. Log past ko waisa nahi yaad rakhte jaisa wo tha, balki uski ek saaf-suthri, perfect (sanitized/idealized) version ko yaad karte hain. Is chakkar mein wo aaj ke waqt mein ek jagah ruk jate hain aur unki mental growth band (stasis/stagnation) ho jati hai. 'repulsive' (ghinauna) trap nahi ho sakta, trap hamesha seductive hota hai.
trick: Nostalgia ek trap hai jo attract karta hai (seductive). Log bure past ko yaad nahi karte, wo use 'clean' kar dete hain (sanitized). Growth rukne ko 'stasis' bolte hain.
tip: Stasis ka matlab hai a state of inactivity or stagnation, jahan koi progress na ho.

question: Direction: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate set of words to make the sentence contextually and grammatically meaningful. || Question: The manager's supposedly open-door policy was entirely ______; employees quickly learned that expressing any genuinely ______ opinions would inevitably result in subtle, yet devastating, professional retaliation.
explanation: Manager ki open-door policy (sabki baat sunne ka claim) poori tarah jhoothi/bhram (illusory) thi. Employees samajh gaye the ki agar unhone aisi raye di jo manager se alag/virodhi (dissenting) hai, toh unka career kharab kiya jayega (professional retaliation). 'tangible, compliant' galat hai kyunki 'compliant' (agree karne wale) opinions par retaliation (badla) nahi liya jata.
trick: 'Supposedly' aur 'retaliation' dikhate hain ki claim fake (illusory) hai aur manager dusro ke virodh (dissent) ko bardaasht nahi kar sakta.
tip: Dissenting opinions ka matlab hai aisi raye jo majority ya boss ke decision ke khilaf ho.
